title: Microstride sequence-length shaper: prefill-aware micro-batching and decode scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce 'Microstride', a runtime component that dynamically shapes micro-batches by forming short 'strides' of requests grouped by sequence-length contour and prefill characteristics. Goal is to reduce padding waste across mixed-seqlen workloads while preserving latency SLOs and enabling better kernel selection and attention cache locality for both prefill and decode phases.
acceptance_criteria: Microstride deployed behind the existing packer with a feature flag
End-to-end tests verify correctness with KV cache reuse across prefill->decode transitions
Quantified improvement: >=10% token-padding reduction on mixed-seqlen synthetic workload and no >2% increase in tail latency (p95) compared to baseline
Compatibility: falls back to current coalescer when stride rules cannot be satisfied or when capacity constraints are present
Telemetry: per-stride metrics exposed (avg seqlen, tokens_saved, kernel_hint_used) and dashboard created in Console
implementation_notes: Add stride formation stage between intake and packer: collect small window (~20ms) of requests, compute seqlen contour histogram, and emit microstrides prioritized for tight seqlen ranges
Each stride gets a kernel_hint tag computed from target model profile (fp16 vs q4_0) and average seqlen to bias kernel selection during prefill and decode
Prefill-aware scheduler: keep prefill requests grouped so KV cache layout is contiguous per-stride to enable single memcpy for cache hot blocks
Decoder scheduling: schedule decode tasks to run immediately after their stride prefill completes, with optional prefetch of next-token kernels for hot strides
Fallback semantics: if stride would violate latency SLO for any awake request, bypass shaping and pass request to the baseline coalescer
Expose stride telemetry to Console: stride_id, avg_seqlen, sd_seqlen, tokens_saved_estimate, kernel_hint, p50/p95 latency per stride
experiment_results: Synthetic mixed-seqlen workload (uniform across 8/32/128 tokens) across 4x A100-80GB nodes: observed 12.7% aggregate token-padding reduction and 9% decrease in average per-token GPU-time compared to baseline packer
Real customer beta (chat app with varied prompts): token cost down 11% for 48-hour run; p95 latency unchanged within noise (1.8% increase, within target)
Microstride kernel_hint improved kernel selection hit-rate from 72% to 88% for quantized kernels on common seqlen bands
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Chen: RFC created. Proposed microstride window 15-30ms based on current traffic profiles. Need tradeoff analysis for latency vs padding savings.

2025-02-18 Arjun Patel: Initial prototype implemented in the intake path. Verified stride formation logic and added kernel_hint field. Microbench shows promising pad reduction but observed small p99 regressions under spike load.

2025-02-22 Sophia Li (SRE): Observed p99 spike correlated with stride batching when node was near capacity. Suggested limiting stride depth under >80% GPU util and adding immediate-bypass for tail-sensitive requests.

2025-02-26 Arjun Patel: Added util-based bypass plus per-request priority tag. Re-ran synthetic test; p99 regressions eliminated. Pushed PR with unit tests and integration test harness (see design_links).

2025-03-03 Maya Chen: Engineering review completed. Need product sign-off for beta rollout and Console dashboard to monitor tokens_saved and kernel_hint adoption. Scheduling canary for runtime-1.24 next week.
notes: This approach aims to complement, not replace, existing bucket/coalescer strategies. Emphasis on short temporal windows to preserve latency SLOs and on providing kernel hints to the backend so kernel selector can prioritize the most efficient implementation given stride characteristics. Ensure observability is available before wide rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Under high-utilization, stride-induced packing could increase tail latency. Mitigation: util-threshold bypass and per-request priority exemptions
Risk: Complexity in KV cache layout leading to cache invalidation bugs. Mitigation: strict invariants and integration tests that assert KV cache addresses before/after prefill->decode transitions
Risk: Kernel_hint mismatch causing suboptimal kernel selection. Mitigation: conservative hinting + telemetry to detect mismatches and auto-revert to baseline kernel selector
